questions.prompt: The founding principle of toxicology, often summarized as "the dose makes the poison," was articulated by:
questions.explanation: Paracelsus, a 16th-century physician, is credited with the foundational toxicological principle that any substance can be toxic depending on dose.

questions.prompt: LD50 refers to the dose of a substance that is:

options.text: Lethal to 50% of a test population
Effective in 50% of a test population

questions.explanation: LD50 (median lethal dose) is the dose required to kill 50% of a tested population, a standard measure of acute toxicity.

questions.prompt: The branch of toxicology concerned with the effects of toxic substances on ecosystems is called:
questions.explanation: Ecotoxicology studies the effects of toxicants on populations and ecosystems, not just individual organisms.

questions.prompt: The capacity of a substance to cause cancer is referred to as its:
questions.explanation: Carcinogenicity describes a substance's potential to cause cancer.

questions.prompt: The liver's primary toxicological role is:
questions.explanation: The liver is the primary site of xenobiotic biotransformation, converting foreign substances into forms that can be excreted.

options.text: The rapid excretion of a substance from an organism
The buildup of a substance in an organism faster than it can be eliminated
The breakdown of a substance into harmless byproducts
The dilution of a substance across a population

questions.explanation: Bioaccumulation occurs when an organism absorbs a substance at a rate faster than it is metabolized or excreted, leading to a buildup over time.

questions.prompt: Acute toxicity refers to adverse effects that occur:

options.text: Within a short period after a single or short-term exposure

questions.explanation: Acute toxicity describes adverse effects arising shortly after a single or short-duration exposure to a substance.

questions.prompt: The highest dose at which no observable adverse effect occurs is termed the:
questions.explanation: The No Observed Effect Level (NOEL) is the highest tested dose at which no adverse effect is detected in a study population.
